claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is in a disordered solid-solution state.
Annealing at 1100 °C for 24–48 hours followed by controlled cooling will enhance short-range chemical order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Variation in short-range chemical order alters local bonding.
Variation in short-range chemical order alters local lattice distortion.
Enhanced short-range chemical order modifies local atomic arrangements and thereby affects dislocation mobility.
Enhanced short-range chemical order alters bond stiffness.
Enhanced short-range chemical order alters vibrational modes.
SRO-induced changes in local atomic arrangements modify activation energies for dislocation motion.
SRO-induced changes in bonding and vibrational modes modify lattice dynamics.
Annealed samples with enhanced SRO will exhibit a measurable shift in yield strength relative to the as-cast baseline.
The yield-strength shift may be either strengthening or softening depending on the barriers produced by SRO.
Annealed samples with enhanced SRO will exhibit a modified temperature dependence of their elastic moduli relative to the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples with enhanced SRO will exhibit an altered, possibly reduced, coefficient of thermal expansion relative to the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast baseline is representative of standard high-temperature behavior without enhanced SRO.
Between 600 and 1000 °C, atomic mobility is sufficient to affect SRO development in HfNbTaTiZr.
HfNbTaTiZr does not undergo large-scale phase transformations over the proposed 600–1000 °C test range.
